newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MADDUX CONTINUES STREAK WITH WIN OVER PADRES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MADDUX CONTINUES STREAK WITH WIN OVER PADRES.

text.p: Greg Maddux and the Braves beat the rain and the Padres on Sunday as Atlanta took a 2-0 rain-shortened victory over San Diego to maintain their major league best record by completing a three-game sweep.
Maddux allowed just one hit and Chipper Jones accounted for the game's only runs with a two-out, two-run double in the third in a game called after the 4 1/2 inning minimum.
Maddux (3-1) has not allowed an earned run in 29 innings and Atlanta won their sixth in a row and 11th in 12 games at Turner Field as they improved their season record to 17-5.
"We knew the rain was coming, we thought we had a couple of hours, but it came sooner," said Braves manager Bobby Cox.
"Just trying to pitch, man, really just go pitch," said Maddux. "I don't know what to say, the weather has been to a pitcher's advantage."
The Braves had runners on first and second and one out in the bottom of the fifth when rain delayed play. After a two-hour and seven-minute wait, the game was called.
San Diego's Tony Gwynn was 0-for-2, snapping his 12-game hitting streak.

In Houston, Damon Berryhill's one-hop single over the head of first baseman Jeff Bagwell scored J.T. Snow with the go-ahead run in the top of the seventh as the San Francisco Giants edged the Houston Astros 3-2.
"It was an ugly at-bat," Berryhill said of his decisive hit against Astros starter Shane Reynolds (3-2).

"He threw me two hard splitters down and I just told myself to stay back on the next one. I was able to get enough of it to get a base hit. It makes it easy when the infield is in and you get that bounce."
San Francisco starter Osvaldo Hernandez (3-1) notched the victory as the surprising Giants improved to 16-5.

At Florida, Edgar Renteria's one-out single in the bottom of the ninth scored Cliff Floyd just ahead of Raul Mondesi's throw as the Florida Marlins completed a three-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers with a 4-3 victory.

With Floyd on second after a double, Renteria bounced a 2-2 pitch into right field. Mondesi, who has one of the strongest throwing arms in baseball, threw up the first-base line but catcher Mike Piazza's tag attempt was just late.
Mark Hutton (2-1) notched the victory, despite allowing a run in the eighth.
Piazza and Mondesi had solo homers for the Dodgers, who have dropped six of their last seven games.
In Montreal, Rey Ordonez delivered a bases-loaded single in the top of the 10th inning as the New York Mets defeated Montreal 5-3 to end the Expos' six-game winning streak.
The 10th inning runs off reliever Lee Smith were the first runs Smith has ever allowed at Olympic Stadium, spanning 23 games and 26 innings.
Greg McMichael (1-2) pitched three scoreless innings and recorded a career-high six strikeouts for his first win as a Met. John Franco worked a perfect 10th for his fourth save.

In St Louis, Donovan Osborne allowed five hits over seven innings and Delino DeShields and Ray Lankford had two-run singles as the St Louis Cardinals ended the Colorado Rockies' team-record eight-game road winning streak with a 6-2 victory.
Gary Gaetti also singled home a run in a five-run second inning and scored in the seventh for the Cardinals, who snapped a three-game losing streak.
Osborne (1-2) struck out six and walked two.

In Chicago, Jason Schmidt combined with two relievers on a five-hitter and had two hits, including an RBI double in the seventh inning, to lead the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 7-0 victory over the Chicago Cubs.
Kevin Elster homered and drove in three runs to boost the Pirates' attack.
Schmidt (1-1) carried a no-hitter into the sixth before Dave Hansen singled.
In Cincinnati, the game between the Philadelphia Phillies and the Reds was postponed due to rain.
